blocks.text: Imagine trying to change a single line of code in a large software system, only to find that it breaks multiple unrelated parts. This is often due to poor coupling and cohesion.

blocks.markdown: In software engineering, coupling and cohesion are two fundamental principles that determine the quality and maintainability of a software system. Coupling refers to the degree of interdependence between software modules, while cohesion refers to the degree to which the elements within a module belong together.

blocks.title: Coupling
blocks.text: Coupling is the measure of how closely connected two routines or modules are. It is a qualitative indication of the degree to which a module relies on other modules.

blocks.title: Cohesion
blocks.text: Cohesion refers to how closely related the functions within a single module are. High cohesion means that the module's responsibilities are closely related and focused.

blocks.markdown: A well-designed system aims to have low coupling and high cohesion. This makes the system easier to understand, maintain, and extend.

blocks.title: Improving Cohesion
blocks.prompt: A module handles both user authentication and data processing. How can you refactor it to improve cohesion?

steps.text: Identify distinct responsibilities: authentication and data processing.
Separate into two modules: one for authentication and another for data processing.

blocks.answer: Refactor by creating two modules: one dedicated to authentication and another to data processing.

blocks.title: Key Point
blocks.text: Strive for low coupling and high cohesion to enhance the maintainability and flexibility of software systems.

points: Coupling and cohesion are crucial for software design quality.
Low coupling and high cohesion lead to more maintainable and flexible systems.
